key_insight: MedGuards frames medical error detection and correction as a multi-agent LLM workflow, using specialized agents plus confidence-based arbitration to improve reliability without retraining the base model.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help reduce unsafe text errors in clinical notes and other healthcare-generated content, supporting safer LLM use in medical settings.
method: Separate agents handle error detection, localization, and correction.
A confidence-guided arbitration step resolves disagreements using reasoning traces and confidence scores.
The system operates as in-context learning, avoiding additional training of the underlying LLMs.
evidence_signal: The authors report improvements across four multilingual clinical-note datasets using multiple models and several evaluation metrics, including the new Keyword-Prioritized Correction Score (KPCS).
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of confidence estimates and reasoning traces, so real-world deployment still needs careful validation across institutions and document types.
paper_title: MedGuards: Multi-Agent System for Reliable Medical Error Detection and Correction
